methods.description: Interpret known amounts as parts of a whole. Add known parts to find their total; subtract a known part or combined parts from the whole or target to find the missing part. Keep the story units.
Start from the known amount and follow the story changes in order. Add amounts received or entering, and subtract amounts removed or used; each result is the amount before the next change.

Identify the two amounts being compared. Subtract the smaller from the larger to find how much more; if a smaller amount and difference are given, add them to find the larger. Combine component totals first when required.

When the amount at the start is unknown but the final amount and changes are given, work backwards. Undo the last change first: add back a loss and subtract an increase. This is an elementary adaptation of the source additive stories, not an algebraic method or filled original inverse example.
